clue.text: Where writers, though poor, need not starve?

definitions.text: Where writers, though poor, need not starve?

parts.words: Where writers, though poor, need not starve?
parts.note: the London street of hack writers is read as a street full of food, since grub is slang for something to eat

explanation.surface: A wistful question about a place where struggling authors are spared hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: The old London street of poor hack writers sounds as if its name promises a meal, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a London street where needy hack writers lived, and now a byword for literary hackwork.

clue.text: Horseman captures a hostile attacker

indicators.note: the horseman holds the letter inside himself, as a captor would hold a prisoner

parts.note: a horseman is a rider

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier seizes an enemy who has come to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who makes a hostile incursion or assault.

clue.text: Such breeches for a county family?

parts.note: Bucks is the usual short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A question about which trousers suit a family of county gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: BUCKS is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London; 'county family' also suggests landed gentry who would wear riding breeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding breeches were commonly made of soft deer leather, hence called by that material's name.

clue.text: Could be right about stern old lyric poet

indicators.note: these words signal that the letters given could be rearranged into another order

parts.note: dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: Speculation that a severe ancient poet might have been correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' is the anagram signal; 'stern' looks like part of a boat but is the adjective, and 'old' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubadours were medieval Provençal poets who composed and sang lyric verse about courtly love.

clue.text: Subject to capital loss, complete the deed

definitions.meaning: to put someone to death, losing their head, the capital part of the body
in law, one signs and seals a deed to make it valid

explanation.surface: A grim instruction mixing punishment by beheading with finishing a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both carrying out a death sentence and formally signing a legal document to make it binding.

clue.text: One of the leading characters in "The Hammer of Revenge"

definitions.text: One of the leading characters in "The Hammer of Revenge"

indicators.note: the leading characters of the title words are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A remark about the cast of a revenge drama with a hammer in its title.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norse thunder god wields the hammer Mjölnir, so he really is a leading figure in any tale of a vengeful hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder, famed for his mighty hammer.

clue.text: European lady of title to study The Constant Nymph

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
Tessa Sanger is the heroine of Margaret Kennedy's 1924 novel The Constant Nymph

explanation.surface: A noblewoman sets out to read a popular romantic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Constant Nymph was a bestselling 1920s novel and play; its heroine is named Tessa.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman holding a noble rank.

clue.text: Notice honey drink in which certain elements are so apportioned

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: the honey drink has the next word placed within it

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from honey
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An advert for a honey drink in which the ingredients are carefully measured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is the container signal; 'elements are so' is the setter saying the pieces are shared out just as the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: To admeasure is an old legal word for to measure out or allot shares.

clue.text: Battle — scene of his last one.

definitions.text: Battle — scene of his last one.

parts.words: Battle — scene of his last one.
parts.note: Battle is the Sussex town at Hastings where the English king died fighting the Normans in 1066

explanation.surface: A terse note about a place that saw someone's final fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle looks like a common noun but is the town built on the site of the 1066 Battle of Hastings, where the last Anglo-Saxon king fell.
explanation.definitionFit: The English king killed at the Battle of Hastings, fought where the town of Battle now stands.

clue.text: Reveal we have a record to be beaten

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose is to be beaten

explanation.surface: An announcement that someone's record is about to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known or expose.

clue.text: Naval craft changes vector to limits of tolerance

indicators.note: the word vector changes into a new order of its letters
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A warship alters its heading as far as it safely can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges VECTOR into CORVET; 'limits of' takes T and E from tolerance.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small, fast warship used for escort duties.

clue.text: Sounds like the end of a Toulouse journey

indicators.note: these words say the following piece is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the painter Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec: what follows Toulouse in his name ends in the syllable trec

explanation.surface: Apparently the final stage of a trip to the French city of Toulouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Toulouse looks like the city, but is the first half of the painter Toulouse-Lautrec; the end of his name, -trec, is said like the word for a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey, often on foot.

clue.text: Change partner in Lobster Quadrille and capsize

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns
in Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle dances the Lobster Quadrille with the Gryphon

explanation.surface: A dance instruction from Lewis Carroll's lobster dance, followed by a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change partner' looks like a dance call, but 'Change' gives TURN and the partner is the Mock Turtle from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is an idiom for a boat overturning so its keel shows.

clue.text: An old church's income is quite the opposite

parts.note: tithes were a tenth of produce paid to the church in former times

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a historic church's revenue is the reverse of what was expected.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or exact reverse of something.

clue.text: Strange monster due to be so described

indicators.note: the letters given are put into a strange, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An odd beast deserves to be called by an impressive adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges MONSTER and DUE; a monster would indeed be described with this adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous means huge or awe-inspiring, just the word one might use of a giant beast.

clue.text: Colourful sky-sign by an East End artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
in Bow, a district of London's East End

explanation.surface: A colourful sign in the sky painted by a cockney painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is RA, placed 'in Bow', a working-class district of East London, so an East End artist is RA IN BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc of spectral colours seen in the sky, and in Genesis a sign of God's covenant.

clue.text: Stuck fast one mile above Alabama City

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means placed earlier

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Someone stranded a mile up from a city in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means unable to move, fixed in place.

clue.text: Mythical being, first of all in nearly 100 years

indicators.note: the first letter is placed inside the shortened word
nearly means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a century is a hundred years

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A legendary creature appears for the first time in almost a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts CENTURY to CENTUR; 'first of all' gives A, and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is a creature of Greek myth, half man and half horse.

clue.text: Threefold Art Excursion takes credit, it's said

indicators.note: these words say the letters come from how the preceding phrase is spoken

parts.note: an excursion is a trip, and credit is tick, so the phrase gives trip with tick

explanation.surface: A three-part exhibition outing is paid for on account.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a painting or carving in three hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: Set to love — wretched child's in to give us the shakes

indicators.note: the child is placed inside the set score

parts.note: a tennis set won six-love is VI (Roman six) and O (love, zero)
a brat is a wretched child; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A tennis match collapses when a naughty child wanders in and frightens everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set to love' looks like a lovesick start, but is a tennis set won six games to none: VI and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is a rapid wavering in pitch, a tremulous effect in singing or playing, so a shaking sound.

clue.text: Time to besiege walled city by forest boundary

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so the word for time goes around the city

parts.note: Berlin was divided by the Berlin Wall

explanation.surface: Time runs out for an army laying siege to a fortified city beside the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The walled city is BERLIN, famous for its Wall from 1961 to 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber line is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees do not grow.

clue.text: Knocked (as Pierre would put it) cold

indicators.note: Pierre stands for a French speaker, whose accent changes how an English word sounds

parts.note: knocked means booed or hissed at; in Pierre's mouth that word comes out as issed

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's way of saying something was struck down.
explanation.walkthrough: A French speaker famously leaves the H silent, so the word for booed comes out sounding like the word for chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means chilled or made very cold.

clue.text: Some sudden dearth of present talent to have this effect on absentees?

definitions.text: to have this effect on absentees?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A sudden shortage of talent on hand makes us fonder of those who are away.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue paints the scene: when present talent is lacking, absent people become dearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone loved, as absence makes the heart grow fonder.

clue.text: Defendant's reply about king's breakfast order

parts.note: re means about, concerning
in A. A. Milne's poem The King's Breakfast the king wants a little butter for his bread

explanation.surface: A defendant answers questions concerning what the monarch ordered for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Breakfast is a well-known A. A. Milne poem in which the king asks for butter.
explanation.definitionFit: In old pleading, a rebutter was the defendant's answer to the plaintiff's surrejoinder.

clue.text: Out late with a bird

indicators.note: out means the following word is put out of its usual order

explanation.surface: Someone is out late in the company of a girlfriend or a feathered friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: Assistants pass in fermenting yeast

indicators.note: the pass goes inside the rearranged letters
fermenting means working or bubbling, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Lab helpers walk past a vat of yeast that is working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fermenting' is the anagram signal, making AYTES; 'pass' is the mountain kind, not a verb, and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are helpers or attendants, especially those serving a priest.

clue.text: Book "All About Love" rejected without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters go around the next piece
rejected means the letters are thrown back, read in reverse
the word all goes about, surrounding, the next letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A romance novel turned down because it lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' makes ALOL, 'rejected' turns it to LOLA, and 'without' is the old sense of outside. The book title in quotes is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov's 1955 novel, named after its title character.

clue.text: The major part played by Albert at the Zoo

definitions.text: played by Albert at the Zoo
definitions.meaning: in the comic monologue The Lion and Albert, young Albert is swallowed by a lion at Blackpool Zoo, becoming its portion

explanation.surface: A remark about a starring role taken by a boy called Albert on a zoo trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lion and Albert is a famous Stanley Holloway monologue in which a lion eats a boy named Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the largest portion, from Aesop's fable where the lion takes everything.
